chapter.printed_title: CLASSIFICATION OF ELEMENTS AND PERIODICITY IN PROPERTIES

questions.stem: State Mendeleev's periodic law.
State the modern periodic law. How many groups and how many periods are there in the long form of the periodic table?
In terms of period and group, where would you place the element with Z = 114 in the periodic table?
Write the atomic number of the element that is in the third period and the seventeenth group of the periodic table.
Why do elements in the same group have similar physical and chemical properties?
What are representative elements? Give their valence shell electronic configuration.
An element X has atomic number 34. Give its position in the periodic table.
Which factors give the transition elements their characteristic properties?
The first ionization enthalpy IE₁ of O is less than that of N. Explain why.
In each of the following pairs, which element has the more negative electron gain enthalpy? Explain. (a) N or O.
questions.notes: The printed wording is garbled: 'Which in each pair of elements has a more electronegative gain enthalpy or electron gain enthalpy? Explain'. Read as NCERT's 'more negative electron gain enthalpy'. Parts (a) and (b) are both printed in the stem.

questions.stem: In each of the following pairs, which element has the more negative electron gain enthalpy? Explain. (b) F or Cl.
questions.notes: Same garbled printed wording as part (a).

questions.stem: Write the increasing order of metallic character among the elements B, Al, Mg and K.
What is the screening effect? How is it related to ionization enthalpy (IE)?
What is a diagonal relationship? Give one pair of elements that show this relationship.
The radii of the iron atom and its ions follow the order Fe > Fe²⁺ > Fe³⁺. Explain.
Why are the zero group elements called noble gases or inert gases?
What is a periodic property? Explain how atomic radius varies in a group and in a period.
questions.notes: Printed as 'What is a periodic property? How the following properties vary in a group and in a period? Explain atomic radius.' — only atomic radius is asked here.

questions.stem: What are isoelectronic species?
questions.notes: Read as two asterisks (**17) before the question number.

questions.stem: Arrange the following species in increasing order of ionic radius: N³⁻, O²⁻, F⁻, Na⁺, Mg²⁺ and Al³⁺.
What is an amphoteric oxide? Give the formula of an amphoteric oxide formed by an element of group 13.
What is lanthanide contraction? Give one of its consequences.
Mg²⁺ is smaller than O²⁻ in size even though both have the same electronic configuration. Explain.
questions.notes: The book prints the ions as Mg⁺² and O⁻² (charge sign before the number).

questions.stem: Give any four characteristic properties of transition elements.
What are rare earths and what are transuranic elements?
What is the valency of an element? How does valency with respect to hydrogen vary across the third period?
Write an essay on the s, p, d and f block elements.
What is a periodic property? Explain how the following property varies in a group and in a period: (a) atomic radius.
questions.notes: Printed as one question with four sub-parts (a)–(d) sharing the preamble 'What is a periodic property? How the following properties vary in a group and in a period? Explain'.

questions.stem: What is a periodic property? Explain how the following property varies in a group and in a period: (b) electron gain enthalpy.
What is a periodic property? Explain how the following property varies in a group and in a period: (c) electronegativity.
What is a periodic property? Explain how the following property varies in a group and in a period: (d) ionization enthalpy.
Define IE₁ and IE₂. Why is IE₂ > IE₁ for a given atom? Discuss the factors that affect the ionization enthalpy (IE) of an element.
questions.notes: The book prints 'the factors that effect IE' (typo for 'affect').

questions.stem: What is a periodic property? Explain how the following property varies in a group and in a period: (b) electron gain enthalpy.
questions.notes: The printed sub-parts are labelled (b), (c), (d) — there is no (a). This question repeats parts (b)–(d) of LAQ 25 with the same preamble.

questions.stem: What is a periodic property? Explain how the following property varies in a group and in a period: (c) electronegativity.
What is a periodic property? Explain how the following property varies in a group and in a period: (d) ionization enthalpy.
Explain the following: (a) valency.
questions.notes: Printed as 'Explain the following: a) Valency b) Diagonal relation and c) Variation of nature of oxides'.

questions.stem: Explain the following: (b) diagonal relationship.
Explain the following: (c) variation of the nature of oxides.
What would be the IUPAC name and symbol of the element with atomic number 120?
questions.notes: Printed label 2.1 (NCERT intext numbering) under the heading INTEXT SOLVED PROBLEMS.

questions.stem: The elements with Z = 117 and Z = 120 have not yet been discovered. In which family or group would you place each of these elements? Also give the electronic configuration in each case.
questions.notes: Printed label 2.3.

questions.notes: Printed label 2.4.

questions.stem: Which of the following species has the largest size and which has the smallest? Mg, Mg²⁺, Al, Al³⁺.
questions.notes: Printed label 2.5.

questions.stem: The first ionization enthalpy values of the third-period elements Na, Mg and Si are 496, 737 and 786 kJ mol⁻¹ respectively. Predict whether the first ionization enthalpy value for Al will be closer to 574 or to 760 kJ mol⁻¹. Justify your answer.
questions.notes: Printed label 2.6. The book prints the unit as 'KJ.mol⁻¹' and writes 'the first ΔH₁ values for Al' where NCERT has ΔᵢH (first ionization enthalpy). The printed '574 (or) 760' is a choice between two candidate values, not two questions.

questions.stem: Which of the following will have the most negative electron gain enthalpy and which the least negative? P, S, Cl, F. Explain your answer.
questions.notes: Printed label 2.7; 'Exaplain' is a printed typo.
